body:
## Requirements check against #1: not all requirements are delivered

I checked out `issue-1-b188f503edf3` (HEAD `60cdd96`), ran the sanitizer suites (106/106 pass), and probed `createSanitizer({})` (default async engine with Secretlint) on realistic inputs. Most of the research and case-study work is done well. But several core requirements are either not met or only met as "documented limitation". In several places the PR redefines the requirement instead of implementing it (for example "no claim of superiority" and "popularity is not inferred automatically"). The issue says to keep going "until each and every requirement fully addressed", so please continue in this PR.

### 1. Partial credential leaks: redacted output still contains part of the secret (critical)

These are correctness bugs in the main feature, because the output still contains part of the secret:

| Input | Output | Leaked |
|---|---|---|
| `Password: Tr0ub4dor&3` | `Password: [REDACTED]&3` | `&3` |
| `pwd: my secret phrase` | `pwd: [REDACTED] secret phrase` | `secret phrase` |
| `{"password":"a\"b"}` | `{"password":"[REDACTED]"b"}` | `b` (escaped quote in a JSON string ends the match) |

The value grammar stops at `&` and whitespace even outside a URL query, and it does not handle escaped quotes inside JSON strings. Please add regression tests for each case. A credential span must cover the whole value up to the real syntactic terminator for its context (end of line for `label: value` prose/YAML, closing unescaped quote for JSON/quoted values).

### 2. "Credentials which are clear from context" are mostly not detected

The issue asks for all credentials whose meaning is clear from context. None of these are detected (output was unchanged):

- `the password is hunter2 for the server` (prose)
- `пароль от сервера: qwerty123` (Russian prose; the 17-language support covers only `label=value` / `label: value` adjacency)
- `export PASS=xyz`, `DB_PASS=short1` (`PASS`/`*_PASS` are not labels; `pwd`, `passwd` are, but common env names like `PASS`, `PASSPHRASE`, `*_PW`, `CREDENTIALS` are missing)
- `mysql -u root -pS3cret`, `sshpass -p hunter2 ssh host` (well-known CLI password flags)
- `api key is ABCDEF1234567890XYZ`

Needed: context detection for "<credential word> is/was/= / : <value>" in prose for every supported language, a wider label vocabulary (env-var naming conventions), and known CLI password flags (`mysql -p`, `sshpass -p`, `PGPASSWORD`, `curl -u user:pass`, `--password`, `-P`, etc.).

### 3. Personal data: names are not detected at all by default

- `Yesterday John Smith from Acme called me…` → unchanged
- `Вчера мне позвонил Иван Петров из компании Ромашка.` → unchanged

Names are only detected after a label (`name: …`) or via the optional Python Presidio bridge, which is off by default and was only exercised with an English model. The issue's first personal-data example is **names**. The library/CLI should detect names in free text by default, in multiple languages. This could be a bundled JS/WASM NER model, a name dictionary/gazetteer, or at least a first-class supported default NER path, with tests per language.

Other common personal data that is not detected (all unchanged):
- National-format phones: `8 (912) 345-67-89`, `(415) 555-2671` (only `+`-prefixed numbers work)
- Postal addresses in prose: `221B Baker Street, London NW1 6XE`
- IBAN: `DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00`
- National IDs without an exact English label: `паспорт 4509 123456`, `my inn is 7707083893` (`паспорт`/`инн` are in the label list, but these were not redacted)
- MAC addresses, messenger handles (`@username`)
- **Usernames in home paths** in logs and AI sessions: `/Users/johnsmith/...`, `/home/alice/.ssh/id_rsa`. This leaks constantly in AI session logs, which the issue names explicitly.

### 4. "Smart" handling of public people, organizations and public emails is not implemented

The issue asks the tool to treat public figures, public organizations and organization-published emails as non-personal **smartly**. The PR only supports a manual allowlist (`publicEntities`) where the caller must supply each exact value plus an HTTPS source and a review date. In the PR's own words, "popularity is not inferred automatically". With default settings:
- `Contact press@microsoft.com` → `Contact [REDACTED]` (an organization's public press address)
- `8.8.8.8` (Google public DNS) → `[REDACTED]`

Needed: a built-in way to tell public from private. Options: a bundled or updatable knowledge base of well-known public people and organizations (for example from Wikidata), role or organization-domain email heuristics (`press@`, `support@`, `info@` on the organization's own domain), public IP ranges (well-known resolvers, documentation ranges), and an optional online verification mode. Keep the current manual policy as an override.

### 5. "Bet exactly all open-source competitors" / "use all algorithms from competitors": not done

The PR says this cannot be certified and only adds a *benchmark plan* (`COMPETITORS.md`, "Benchmark plan for the market-wide aspiration"). Concretely missing:
- **No benchmark was run.** There is no labelled corpus and no recall/precision comparison against Gitleaks, TruffleHog, detect-secrets, Presidio, scrubadub, etc. Without one there is no evidence for "most robust on the market". Please add the corpus and a reproducible benchmark script, publish results in the case study, and iterate until the default configuration matches or beats each competitor on that corpus.
- **Competitor rules are not ported.** The default engine has 26 native provider families plus the Secretlint recommended preset. Gitleaks alone ships ~200+ rules and TruffleHog ~800 detectors, but they are only used if the user installs the binaries separately (`--gitleaks`, `--trufflehog`). They were not even present in this environment. To "use all algorithms from competitors", port their rule sets (Gitleaks' TOML rules are MIT and straightforward to import) into the default engine, with a sync/update script.
- detect-secrets plugins (keyword detector, high-entropy base64/hex strings), scrubadub detectors and Presidio recognizers (IBAN, national IDs for many countries, crypto wallets, medical license, etc.) are not reimplemented natively.
- Examples of known formats missed by default: GitLab runner registration token (`GR1348941…`), Firebase/FCM server key (`AAAA…:APA91b…`).

### 6. Closed-source competitors: features not supported

The issue says to "use their docs and examples to support all their features as well". The PR only adds a generic offset-report adapter, so users can import results *from* Google DLP / Azure / AWS / GitGuardian. Their documented features are listed as "Remaining feature gap": the infoType catalog (Google DLP has 150+ infoTypes), de-identification transforms (masking with partial reveal, format-preserving/deterministic pseudonymization, date shifting, bucketing), and per-type confidence/likelihood. Please implement the documented infoTypes/entity types natively and add at least the common transformation modes. Today the only mode is full `[REDACTED]`.

### 7. Not all of our existing practices were collected and carried over

`REPOSITORY-RESEARCH.md` covers hive-mind, but several hive-mind features documented in [`docs/CREDENTIAL-SANITIZATION.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/CREDENTIAL-SANITIZATION.md) and its modules are missing here:
- **Streaming sanitization** (`log-sanitize-stream.lib.mjs`, record buffering so a credential split across chunks is not emitted, held-back base64 line groups) and **bounded worker** sanitization (`log-sanitize-worker*.mjs`). This package has no streaming API: logs larger than 10 MiB are rejected instead of processed.
- **HTML-entity and byte-escape decoding.** A GitHub token encoded as `ghp…` or `\x67\x68\x70…` passes through unchanged here, but hive-mind decodes both.
- **Mask contract `abc…xyz`** (keep first/last 3 chars for values longer than 12) and **re-encoding of masked payloads** so base64/JSON structure stays valid. Here the whole encoded blob becomes `[REDACTED]`. At least offer it as an option, because our tooling and logs depend on it.
- **Exact values from local GitHub auth (`gh auth token`)**. This is deliberately excluded here, but hive-mind relies on it. Make it an opt-in.
- The `require-sanitized-output` ESLint rule and outbound-boundary integration (Sentry payload sanitization, `instrument.sanitize.lib.mjs`). These are reusable practices that should be offered by this framework (for example an ESLint plugin export and a Sentry `beforeSend` helper).

### 8. Git history: only an audit, no redaction or editing tool

The issue says "tools to carefully redact / edit history". The PR adds a read-only `history` audit and a manual `git filter-repo` procedure in docs. Please add a `history rewrite` (or similar) command. It should generate the replacement/mailmap files from the audit's findings, run on a fresh clone by default with a dry-run/preview, and re-audit the result. Force-push should still be a separate explicit step.

### 9. Natural languages: coverage is thin

17 languages have one or two credential label words each, and a handful of PII labels. Nothing handles language specifics (morphology/inflection such as `пароля`/`паролем`, word order in prose, non-Latin digit systems like Arabic-Indic or Devanagari digits in phones/IDs, locale date formats, transliteration of names). Please expand the vocabularies (inflected forms), add per-language prose context rules, and add test fixtures per language for each personal-data type, not only credential labels.

### 10. Minor

- The package root still exports template helpers `add`, `multiply` and `delay`, and ships the `example-package-name` bin. These have nothing to do with a sanitizer package. Consider removing them or moving them out of the public API.
- `docs/` still contains template-era files (`ISSUE-199-RELEASE-ANALYSIS.md`, `ISSUE-203-ANALYSIS.md`, `CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md`) that are unrelated to this project.

### Reproduction

All results above come from the default async engine:

```js
import { createSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const engine = await createSanitizer({});
console.log((await engine.sanitize('Password: Tr0ub4dor&3')).text); // Password: [REDACTED]&3
```

Please add every input listed in this comment as a regression fixture (expected: fully redacted, or preserved for the public cases), then continue the implementation until they pass.
